title_en: Yellow River Film and Television Studio v. Linyi County TV Station — copyright infringement dispute

full_text_en:
Yellow River Film and Television Studio v. Linyi County Television Station — copyright infringement dispute

Plaintiff: Shanxi Province Yellow River Film and Television Studio.

Legal Representative: Kong Lingyun, Director.

Agents ad litem: Wang Jian and Zhao Ping, lawyers from Yuncheng Modern Law Firm, Shanxi Province.

Defendant: Shanxi Province Linyi County Television Station.

Legal Representative: Fan Zhongzhao, Station Director.

Agent ad litem: Wang Yanrong, Deputy Director of Shanxi Province Linyi County Television Station.

Agent ad litem: Wang Wenzhi, lawyer from Shanxi Province Linyi County Law Firm.

The plaintiff, Shanxi Province Yellow River Film and Television Studio (hereinafter referred to as the Film Studio), filed a lawsuit with the Yuncheng Intermediate People's Court of Shanxi Province against the defendant, Shanxi Province Linyi County Television Station (hereinafter referred to as the County TV Station), regarding a copyright infringement dispute.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The defendant, without authorization, illegally copied and broadcasted via its station the Puju opera TV series "The West Chamber," for which the plaintiff holds the wireless television broadcasting and distribution rights, thereby infringing upon the plaintiff's copyright. The plaintiff requested the court to order the defendant to cease the infringement, eliminate the adverse effects, make a public apology, and compensate for economic losses in the amount of RMB 608,098.

Defendant's Defense: The defendant claimed that it copied the Puju opera TV series "The West Chamber" from CCTV Channel 8 and broadcast it once, in accordance with an agreement with CCTV Channel 8, in order to provide local residents of Linyi County with information about operatic works featuring local characteristics. When CCTV Channel 8 broadcast "The West Chamber," there was no statement indicating "Copyright Reserved. Unauthorized Reproduction Prohibited." Whether viewed from the perspective of the facts themselves or from the rights protected under copyright law, this matter is solely between the defendant and CCTV Channel 8 and has nothing to do with the plaintiff. The court should dismiss the plaintiff's lawsuit.

Facts Found by the Yuncheng Intermediate People's Court: The five-episode Puju opera TV series "The West Chamber" was a videographic work jointly invested in and co-produced by the plaintiff, the Film Studio, and the CCTV Film and Television Department. In March 1997, the Film Studio and the CCTV Film and Television Department signed an agreement stipulating that the wireless television broadcasting and distribution rights for the series belonged to the Film Studio, with all proceeds accruing to the Film Studio; the copyright and copyright proceeds for cable television belonged to the CCTV Film and Television Department. After the filming of "The West Chamber" was completed, in order to participate in a national film and television evaluation activity, the two parties agreed that CCTV would broadcast the series on Channel 8 on March 31 and April 2, 1997, respectively. The defendant, the County TV Station, recorded the entire series when it was broadcast on CCTV Channel 8 and subsequently broadcast it on its own wireless television station on May 20 and 27, 1997, during which it also inserted commercial advertisements.

The court further found that between April and May 1997, the plaintiff, the Film Studio, jointly distributed videotapes of the five-episode Puju opera TV series "The West Chamber" with Shanxi Audio-Visual Publishing House. To this end, the Propaganda Department of the Yuncheng Prefectural Party Committee issued a "Notice on Subscribing to Videotapes of the Puju Opera TV Series 'The West Chamber'" on May 18, 1997, requiring all counties and cities in the region to ensure that every factory, mine, government organ, township, village, and cultural station (room) purchase one set, and set the price of each videotape set at RMB 298.

The plaintiff's business scope includes TV dramas, TV specials, TV variety shows, and animation, with business methods including planning, consulting, production, recording, and distribution. The wireless broadcasts of the defendant, the County TV Station, covered not only its own county but also neighboring areas including Yuncheng, Xia County, Pinglu, Yongji, Wenxi, Wanrong, as well as Dali, Hancheng, Chengcheng, etc., in Shaanxi Province.

The above facts are confirmed by evidence including the TV drama co-production agreement, the subscription notice from the Propaganda Department of the Yuncheng Prefectural Party Committee, the advertising card of the County TV Station, and the statistical table of videotape distribution provided by the Film Studio.

Yuncheng Intermediate People's Court: The court held that the plaintiff, the Film Studio, enjoyed the wireless television broadcasting and distribution rights to the five-episode Puju opera TV series "The West Chamber," as well as the right to authorize others to broadcast it and obtain remuneration. The defendant, the County TV Station, without obtaining permission, arbitrarily broadcast the TV series on its wireless television station and used it for profit-making activities, which violated Articles 44 and 45 of the Copyright Law of the PRC and constituted an infringement of the Film Studio's wireless television broadcasting and distribution rights. The County TV Station shall bear civil liability for compensation for the direct losses and loss of expected profits suffered by the Film Studio as a result of this infringement. Accordingly, on August 6, 1998, the court ruled:

The defendant, the County TV Station, shall compensate the plaintiff, the Film Studio, for economic losses in the amount of RMB 600,000.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 11,090 and other litigation costs of RMB 2,120 shall be borne by the defendant, the County TV Station.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, the defendant, the County TV Station, refused to accept it and appealed to the Shanxi High People's Court. The grounds for appeal were as follows: A videographic work is an audiovisual work, and reproduction requires access to the original recording of the work. The appellant never had access to the original recording, therefore there was no reproduction. Article 46 of the Copyright Law of the PRC separately provides for the reproduction of videographic works and the reproduction of television programs under paragraphs (5) and (6), which demonstrates that these are two different legal concepts and two different types of conduct. The appellant only recorded the television program "The West Chamber" by converting the electrical signal into a magnetic signal when it was broadcast by CCTV, in accordance with an agreement with CCTV for the paid use of its encrypted channel, and then aired it once to the local public. There was no statement on the broadcast indicating "Copyright Reserved. Unauthorized Reproduction Prohibited." This conduct complies with the provisions of Article 40, paragraph 2 of the Copyright Law of the PRC and does not constitute infringement. The appellant never reproduced the appellee's original recording of "The West Chamber," and therefore there was no infringement of the appellee's copyright. The first-instance judgment, which found the appellant liable for infringement based on the appellee's alleged wireless television broadcasting and distribution rights and in accordance with Articles 44 and 45 of the Copyright Law of the PRC, was based on unclear facts and improper application of law. The appellant requested that the second-instance court set aside the judgment.

The appellee, the Film Studio, responded in defense: The five-episode Puju opera TV series "The West Chamber" was a videographic work jointly filmed by the appellee with an investment of RMB 1.9 million and by CCTV with an investment of RMB 200,000. Because the appellant, without authorization, publicly broadcast the series on its wireless television station, the appellee was unable to properly exercise its wireless television broadcasting licensing rights and videotape distribution rights, resulting in significant economic losses for which the appellant should bear compensation liability. A television program refers to items broadcast by a television station, encompassing various forms of broadcast content, which naturally includes videographic works. Although television programs include videographic works, they are not equivalent to them. A videographic work does not cease to be a videographic work simply because it is broadcast by a television station, nor does it cease to be protected by the Copyright Law of the PRC. The appellant's argument that videographic works and television programs are two different concepts and therefore there is no infringement is untenable. The appellant repeatedly claimed that it had an agreement with CCTV allowing it to use the television programs broadcast by that station for a fee; this is not true. CCTV has never entered into such an agreement with any wireless television station. The first-instance finding that the appellant constituted infringement and the award of damages were correct and should be upheld.

Shanxi High People's Court, Second Instance: The court found the following additional facts:

On December 11, 1996, Shanxi Radio and Television Consulting Service Center, as the authorized general agent for Shanxi recognized by the Central Satellite Television Transmission Center (Party A to the contract), and the appellant, the County TV Station (Party B to the contract), signed a one-year "Central Satellite Scrambled TV Program Viewing Agreement" in Taiyuan. The agreement stipulated: Party A shall provide Party B with decryption equipment and technical services for the four scrambled TV programs of CCTV; Party B shall receive and descramble the Central Satellite Scrambled TV programs and transmit them to end users within its system, be responsible for collecting viewing fees from users, and provide viewing services. The copyright of the Central Satellite Scrambled TV programs belongs to CCTV; Party B has the right to receive and retransmit the programs within its own network and shall transmit each set of programs in full. Without Party A's permission, Party B shall not reproduce, transfer, or engage in profit-making activities or other infringing conduct with the program content in any form, nor shall it transmit scrambled programs outside its own system without authorization. Other provisions regarding payment and breach of contract are omitted.

The wireless TV coverage area of the appellant, the County TV Station, as found in the first instance, was based on the information in the promotional materials used by the station to attract advertisers. According to measurements by the Science and Technology Department of the Shanxi Provincial Radio and Television Bureau, the normal transmission coverage range of the County TV Station was approximately 25 kilometers, with the specific range depending on the ruggedness of the actual terrain. Because the appellant, the County TV Station, broadcast the five-episode Puju opera TV series "The West Chamber," some viewers who had originally planned to purchase videotapes from the appellee, the Film Studio, no longer did so, resulting in a decrease in videotape sales.

The total screening time of the five-episode Puju opera TV series "The West Chamber" was 3 hours, 47 minutes, and 39 seconds. The appellee, the Film Studio, submitted to the court the "1996 World TV Series and Film Price List," which indicated that the price of Chinese TV series was between USD 1,500 and USD 2,500 per hour.

The above facts are confirmed by evidence including the "Central Satellite Scrambled TV Program Viewing Agreement," the "Forecast of Coverage Area of Xiaoyi Mountain Relay Station in Linyi County," the videotape of the five-episode Puju opera TV series "The West Chamber," the "1996 World TV Series and Film Price List," and witness testimony. Apart from these, the second instance confirmed other facts found in the first instance.

Shanxi High People's Court held:

The appellee, the Film Studio, and the CCTV Film and Television Department jointly invested in and co-produced the five-episode Puju opera TV series "The West Chamber." In accordance with Article 15 of the Copyright Law of the PRC, they jointly enjoy the copyright in this videographic work, other than the right of attribution enjoyed by authors such as the director, screenwriter, lyricist, composer, and cinematographer. According to the agreement between the Film Studio and the CCTV Film and Television Department, the wireless television broadcasting licensing rights and distribution rights in this videographic work belong to the Film Studio, with the proceeds accruing to the Film Studio. The rights enjoyed by the Film Studio are in accordance with the provisions of the Copyright Law of the PRC and shall be protected by law; no one may infringe upon them. Article 44 of the Copyright Law of the PRC provides: "A television station that broadcasts another person's film, television, or video works shall obtain permission from the producer of the film, television, or video work, and pay remuneration." The appellant, the County TV Station, used another person's work without obtaining permission from anyone, which constitutes an infringement. It shall, in accordance with Article 45(5) of the Copyright Law of the PRC, bear civil liability such as ceasing the infringement, eliminating the adverse effects, making a public apology, and compensating for losses. Regardless of whether the County TV Station was aware of the agreement between the Film Studio and CCTV, the Film Studio may, based on that agreement, hold the County TV Station liable for infringement of its wireless television broadcasting licensing rights. The County TV Station's argument that, whether viewed from the perspective of the facts or from the rights protected under copyright law, its recording and broadcasting of "The West Chamber" from CCTV Channel 8 had nothing to do with the Film Studio, is untenable. Because the County TV Station only copied the TV series "The West Chamber" for the purpose of broadcasting and did not distribute the copied videotapes for profit, it did not infringe the Film Studio's distribution rights. The Film Studio's argument that the County TV Station infringed its distribution rights is untenable. However, the County TV Station's broadcasting conduct would inevitably affect the Film Studio's performance in distributing videotapes of the TV series "The West Chamber." The County TV Station shall provide appropriate compensation for the loss of expected profits suffered by the Film Studio as a result of the impact on its distribution rights. Given that the County TV Station's broadcasting had limited impact due to its scale, the amount of compensation for this loss shall be determined by the court at its discretion based on the actual coverage area of the County TV Station and the actual distribution situation of the Film Studio's videotapes.

The distribution and purchase of videotapes are civil acts, and both parties should act on the principle of voluntariness; superior requirements cannot serve as the basis for whether a civil act is performed. Moreover, in fact, due to economic affordability constraints, the various factories, mines, government organs, townships, villages, and cultural stations (rooms) in the Yuncheng area could not possibly meet the purchase requirements set forth in the notice of the Propaganda Department of the Yuncheng Prefectural Party Committee. The first-instance judgment's calculation of the appellee's loss of expected profits based on that notice was inconsistent with reality.

The appellant, the County TV Station, had the right, according to its agreement with the Central Satellite Television Transmission Center, to receive and retransmit TV programs from CCTV Channel 8, but it did not have the right to reproduce them, and certainly not to transmit them to wireless television stations outside its system. The County TV Station's argument that its conduct complied with Article 40, paragraph 2 of the Copyright Law of the PRC, which provides that "a radio station or television station that uses another person's published work to produce a radio or television program may do so without the permission of the copyright owner," is untenable as a defense against infringement.

The facts found in the first instance were generally clear, and the finding that the appellant, the County TV Station, constituted infringement was accurate in characterization, but the judgment was inappropriate and should be amended. The County TV Station's appeal ground that the amount of damages was unreasonable is correct and should be sustained; the other appeal grounds are dismissed. Accordingly, in accordance with Article 153(1)(3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the Shanxi High People's Court, on January 21, 1999, ruled:

1. The first-instance civil judgment is amended as follows: The appellant, the County TV Station, shall compensate the appellee, the Film Studio, for economic losses in the amount of RMB 192,160.

2. The appellant, the County TV Station, shall apologize to the appellee, the Film Studio, and eliminate the adverse effects within the original scope of the infringement.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 11,090 and other litigation costs of RMB 2,120 for the first instance, and litigation costs of RMB 11,090 for the second instance, shall be borne by the appellant, the County TV Station.
